page.title: In the browser
page.description: Run the charts you run on Node.js in a page or a Worker with @tinyactors/wasm, the same API on core compiled to WebAssembly.

hero.headline: Run your actors in a browser
hero.lede: Change one import, and the charts you run on Node.js run in a page or a Worker, on tinyactors compiled to WebAssembly. The same package runs Node.js and Bun where no native addon is built, such as Windows.

section.heading: Import the WebAssembly package instead
section.p: Import @tinyactors/wasm in place of @tinyactors/node, and every other guide holds unchanged. This program logs the same line in a page as in Node.js:

section.heading: Treat bytes as Uint8Arrays, not Buffers
section.p: Where @tinyactors/node gives a Buffer, this package gives a plain Uint8Array. A Buffer is a Uint8Array too, so code written against Uint8Array runs on both.
That covers every output in bytes: compiled.image, host.hibernate(), host.snapshot(), host.metrics(), telemetry and encode().
Decode text with TextDecoder instead of buf.toString(), and copy or compare with the typed array's own methods. This program copies an encoded value and writes it as base64:
index.d.ts, which both packages share, types every one of them as Uint8Array.

section.heading: Call init() under a bundler or Service Worker
section.p: The package's entry loads its module, tinyactors.wasm beside its files, with top-level await. A browser fetches the file, Node.js and Bun read it, and every name works once the import settles.
A Service Worker refuses a module graph with top-level await. Some bundlers neither handle it nor place tinyactors.wasm beside the bundle: esbuild does not follow new URL(..., import.meta.url).
There, import @tinyactors/wasm/init: it exports the same names and init(source?), which loads the module once. Every call made before it settles throws TA_ERROR_STATE.
Give init a URL, a Response, the bytes or a compiled WebAssembly.Module, or nothing to load the package's own file. This program makes a host before and after init():

section.p: The package targets ES2022 and serves the module as @tinyactors/wasm/tinyactors.wasm, so a bundler or a CDN can place it.

section.heading: Target Chrome 114, Firefox 119 and Safari 16.4
section.p: By the engines' release notes, Chrome and Edge 114, Firefox 119 and Safari 16.4 have every feature the package uses. Only Chromium 141 is tested.

item.text: extended-const, multivalue, bulk-memory and nontrapping-fptoint, in the module.
top-level await and String.prototype.isWellFormed, in the package.

section.heading: Allow WebAssembly and eval in your CSP
section.p: The module needs 'wasm-unsafe-eval' in script-src. The default engine, the native datamodel, runs your charts' expressions and scripts as JavaScript, so it needs 'unsafe-eval' too.
Under any of these policies, new Host(...) on the native datamodel throws TinyactorsError with TA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED, its message naming the directive:

item.text: Trusted Types enforced (require-trusted-types-for 'script'), which guards string evaluation even with 'unsafe-eval'.

section.p: Under them, compileCharts also skips its check of the charts' JavaScript syntax, since it parses with the same constructor. Run such a page's charts on quickjs.

section.heading: Run charts on quickjs under a strict policy
section.p: With datamodel: 'quickjs', chart code runs on quickjs-ng inside the package's module, so the page's policy needs only 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. Use it for charts you do not trust, too.
Every quickjs option and behaviour of @tinyactors/node holds here (). This host sets maxOps and reads the engine's heap size:
Every page downloads quickjs, since the one module holds it: 378 KiB with brotli, against 137 KiB without it. mise run pack:wasm reports the sizes.
The engine's stack is the module's, at most 256 KiB whatever quickjs.stackLimit asks. A deeper recursion is its evaluation's error.execution, RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
Inside quickjs, Date reads the real clock, as in @tinyactors/node, whatever clock the host runs on.

section.heading: Declare every variable your scripts assign
section.p: Scripts and expressions run as strict code, so an assignment to a name nobody declared is the script's error.execution. It never becomes a global.
Declare a variable with a top-level var or with <data>. Here the declared chart keeps visits through hibernation, and the undeclared one fails:
Top-level declarations follow the rules of @tinyactors/node (Writing charts):

item.text: a chart-level script's functions are the chart's helpers, made once;
a top-level var is a variable of the session;
let, const and class at a script's top level are refused.

section.p: A host runs its charts in a realm of its own, a set of globals it makes at its first chart. Each actor's variables are a scope object there, and the realm differs by platform:

row.cell: a hidden iframe of the page's origin, one per host, removed at close()
the worker's own global (a Worker has no document)

section.p: A hidden iframe looks like a sandbox but is not one: chart code runs in your engine and must be trusted.

section.heading: Move the charts off the page's thread
section.p: On the page's thread, a chart step that runs long is a frame the page does not draw.
In a dedicated Worker the page stays responsive, and the charts' realm holds none of the page's code. Only values cross postMessage, as between any two systems.
The page waits until the worker says it listens, since a message sent before the worker's module ran is lost. Then it asks for a counter and two visits:
The worker, counters-worker.mjs beside the page, runs the host. It answers each question once the host is idle, with the count the counter sends to urn:page:
A module Worker has no import map. A bundler resolves @tinyactors/wasm in the worker as in the page, or the worker imports the package's index.mjs by its URL.

section.heading: Keep hibernated actors in IndexedDB
section.p: Your code chooses where a browser host's hibernated actors and snapshots live. A browser has no SQLite, so it refuses SQLiteStore ().
A page has IndexedDB, which stores a Uint8Array as it is. The host follows a store's promises, so IndexedDB can be a host's store directly.
This counter is hibernated into IndexedDB, then loaded from it when its next event comes:

section.heading: Expect late timers in a hidden tab
section.p: In Node.js an open host with a pending deadline keeps the process alive. A page's hosts run only while the page does.
A host runs its turns as MessageChannel messages and arms one setTimeout at its next deadline. A browser throttles that timer while the tab is hidden.
Chromium runs a hidden tab's timers about once a second, and once a minute after a few minutes hidden. A dedicated Worker is throttled less, but still throttled.
A delayed <send> or a timeout then comes late, when the timer fires, and is never lost.

section.heading: Snapshot the host when the page hides
section.p: A tab can be closed or discarded without notice, and its actors go with it. Keep what must survive in your store.
Hibernate actors as they go cold, or snapshot the host on visibilitychange, the last event a page is sure to get. Restore the snapshot when the page loads again.
This cart is snapshotted into IndexedDB, and a second load restores it with its item kept:
A snapshot leaves out the services your program runs, which a restore announces again ().

section.heading: Size a page for its peak memory
section.p: The host's memory is the module's linear memory, which grows and is never given back: a page keeps its peak.

item.term: Hibernation makes room, not a smaller page.
item.text: Hibernating actors frees room for others in that memory. A snapshot is packed there before it is copied out, so a 100 MB snapshot leaves the memory 100 MB larger.
wasm32 addresses 4 GiB, and a region that grows is copied before the old one is freed. So one host holds about two million resident actors at most, where @tinyactors/node goes on.

item.term: What the package hands out stays valid.
item.text: Bytes, values and views are never views of that memory, so they stay valid when it grows.

section.p: What one actor costs in that memory is measured in Capacity and memory.

section.heading: Share a database with a Node.js server
section.p: A server on @tinyactors/node and a browser client on @tinyactors/wasm can share a database, but not the bytes a host packs.

item.text: encode and decode are one format in both packages (): move work between the server and the client as events and their data, from one system to another.

It is the host's memory as the build that made it lays it out, and the addon is a 64-bit build where the module is a 32-bit one. Each package labels its snapshots with its own name and refuses the other's with TA_ERROR_INVALID, the message naming the package that made it.

item.term: A hibernation blob belongs to its host.
item.text: It wakes in the host that hibernated it, or in one restored from that host's snapshot, which the other package cannot restore; another host's blob throws TA_ERROR_INVALID. Keep the server's blobs and the client's apart in the store, by host.
